description:
TURUBO is a team from Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia, inspired by the ancient Chiquitano legend of Turubó.

Our mission is to explore how Earth's landscapes can help us understand the Moon and Mars.

By combining NASA's open data, geospatial analysis, and artificial intelligence, we aim to identify and visualize potential terrestrial analog sites, beginning with Bolivia.

From ancient legends to new worlds, we turn curiosity into exploration.
summary:
TURUBO is a bilingual web experience that connects a Chiquitano story from Bolivia with the search for terrestrial analogs of the Moon and Mars. Visitors follow Turubó through a 3D adventure, explore photographs of the Chiquitania and open scientific terrain comparisons without losing their place in the story.

We analyzed 25 fixed, contiguous tiles around the Valle de la Luna of San José de Chiquitos using NASADEM elevation data. We compared them with Nobile Rim 1 on the Moon using NASA LRO/LOLA data, and Jezero crater on Mars using a USGS CTX elevation product. All windows cover 4 × 4 km on a 40 m grid. The ranking uses median slope, P90 slope and P95–P5 relief.

Our closest Jezero candidate has a similar median slope. The closest lunar candidate still has much less relief than Nobile, whose P95–P5 relief is about 2.7 times as large. These results characterize a small regional sample, not landing safety or habitability. Cerro Turubó appears separately as a cultural and geographic reference.

TURUBO makes planetary data accessible through storytelling, while publishing maps, sources, methods and limitations so visitors can examine the evidence themselves. The experience works in English and Spanish on desktop and mobile.
details:
TURUBO connects a Chiquitano story from Bolivia with the challenge to identify and characterize terrestrial terrain analogs. Visitors scroll from the Chiquitania to the Moon and Mars, walk through a short fantasy adventure or open the measured terrain directly. Players use keyboard, click or touch controls, follow a light to three encounters, and choose a response. Illustrated alternatives preserve the adventure without 3D. The fictional scenery is separate from the scientific maps. Cerro Turubó is a separate guided example outside the ranking.

METHOD AND FINDINGS

We fixed 25 tiles of 4 x 4 km around the Valle de la Luna of San José de Chiquitos. Elevation crops were averaged onto a 40 m grid; tiles require at least 95% valid coverage. The ranking uses standardized distance over median slope, P90 slope and P95 minus P5 relief. Same-scale maps show elevation relative to each tile median.

R03 C01 is closest to Nobile Rim 1 within our sample. Nobile has 624.61 m relief and 14.70 degrees median slope, versus 229.61 m and 7.16 degrees in R03 C01. The lunar DEM interpolates numerous heights: full valid grid coverage does not mean direct measurements everywhere. R02 C02 is closest to Jezero. Their median slopes are 1.64 and 2.11 degrees respectively, and relief is 63.38 and 77.56 m. This is a limited regional topographic comparison, not proof of geology, climate, gravity, radiation, resources, habitability or landing safety. Adjacent tiles are not independent regional samples. We propose candidates for further study, not validated mission sites.

TOOLS AND IMPACT

Python, Rasterio, PyProj, NumPy and Pillow prepare reproducible evidence. TypeScript, Vite, Three.js and GSAP power the public bilingual website. A progressive experience works with reduced motion, data saver and without WebGL. Cultural storytelling invites non-specialists to explore planetary data; measurements and sources allow them to question the comparisons. Code, pipeline, credits and licenses: https://github.com/federicorv25/turubo

AI DISCLOSURE

OpenAI Codex assisted with software, tests, vector art, scientific communication and presentation. ChatGPT supported bilingual story editing; Cursor Composer supported the comparison interface. Google AI Studio and Claude Code assisted with Asael Rojas Mansilla's Earth encounter. Federico and Codex extended controls and fictional Moon and Mars sets, labeled as AI-assisted 3D art. Kie.ai Seedream 5.0 Pro generated six visibly labeled narrative illustrations. Documentary photographs are attributed separately. Measurements and rankings come from cited elevation products and reproducible calculations, not model-generated scientific predictions. No model API runs when visitors use the website. Full asset and software credits: https://github.com/federicorv25/turubo/blob/main/submission/credits-en.md
